title: Salesmsg vs Aircall — Jon Martin
seoTitle: Salesmsg vs Aircall for HubSpot Teams
description: Salesmsg and Aircall compared for small HubSpot teams: entry prices, texting vs calling, HubSpot workflows and logging, and seat minimums.
dek: A texting-first tool and a calling-first tool, compared for a small team that wants every conversation on the HubSpot record.
Prices and features below come from each vendor's own pages, checked on the date shown. Both links are affiliate links.

blocks.html: This comparison is for a small sales or service team in {{link:hubspot}} that talks to customers by text and phone, and is choosing between {{link:salesmsg}} and {{link:aircall}}.
Both can text and both can call. The real question is which channel your team uses most, because each tool is built around one of them.

Choose Salesmsg if most conversations happen by text and you want HubSpot workflows to send messages automatically. Choose Aircall if most conversations are calls and you want a full phone system with texting on the side.

For a two-person team, Salesmsg Basic plus one extra seat is about {{calc:salesmsg_two}} a month. Aircall needs three licenses, so its floor on Essentials is about {{calc:aircall_three}} a month on annual billing.

Salesmsg Basic is {{fact:salesmsg.basic}}, and Pro is {{fact:salesmsg.pro}}. Extra seats are {{fact:salesmsg.extra_seat}}, and extra numbers are {{fact:salesmsg.extra_number}}. Messages and minutes use credits: {{fact:salesmsg.credits}}. There's {{fact:salesmsg.trial}}.
In HubSpot, Salesmsg offers {{fact:salesmsg.hubspot}}. It also says {{fact:salesmsg.optout}}.

Aircall Essentials is {{fact:aircall.essentials_annual}}, and Professional is {{fact:aircall.professional_license}}. There's {{fact:aircall.min_licenses_ess_pro}}, and you get {{fact:aircall.annual_saving}}.

sections.label: Fit for a small HubSpot team

blocks.html: If your customers reply to texts and ignore calls, Salesmsg's workflow-triggered texts save the most time: reminders, follow-ups, and confirmations go out without a rep touching them.
If your team lives on the phone, Aircall's call logging and caller context in HubSpot matter more than texting features.
Salesmsg runs on credits, so heavy calling or long texts can cost more than the plan price suggests.
Aircall's three-license minimum makes it a poor fit for one or two people, and texting isn't the center of the product.
Pull last month's conversations and count texts against calls. Buy the tool built for the bigger number.
Whichever you choose, make sure opt-outs reach a single HubSpot property before you send any automated texts.

closing: Pick Salesmsg when texting carries the work and Aircall when calls do.
